name: Plainstrider Beak
summary: Across the Barrens, hunters bring Plainstrider Beaks back to the Crossroads. Huntmasters use them as proof that birds threatening local provisions have been culled.

sections.title: A Measure of the Hunt
sections.body: Plainstriders forage around the Crossroads and threaten its supplies. Greater, fleeting, and ornery plainstriders roam the surrounding savannah. Sergra Darkthorn asks arriving hunters to bring back their beaks as proof that the flocks have been culled away from supply lines and storehouses.

faq.q: Why does Sergra Darkthorn want Plainstrider Beaks?
faq.answer: Sergra Darkthorn asks hunters to cull plainstriders because the birds harass food supplies around the Crossroads. Their beaks show that the hunt has reduced the threat to local supplies.
Hunters take the beaks from greater, fleeting, and ornery plainstriders roaming the Barrens savannah.

faq.q: Why don't all plainstriders provide a beak when slain?
faq.answer: In the struggle, swift, thrashing birds can leave a beak cracked, shattered, or unusable as a clean trophy. Hunters gather only intact beaks.

angles.text: As a hunter, taking down plainstriders and gathering their beaks gives you an early lesson in stalking and securing prey across Kalimdor’s open plains.
As a member of the Horde, culling the nuisance flocks east of the Crossroads helps protect the trade and supply routes that feed the outpost.
